entries.detail: Ran `find` for *.swift across all 8 targets (59 files total), then grepped each for top-level type declarations (class/struct/enum/protocol/actor) and compared to the basename. EntitlementResolver.swift:16 declares exactly one top-level type, `public enum Entitlement`, which contains all nested types (Capability, Tier, ActiveSubscription) and the single static function; there is no second top-level declaration in the 61-line file. The basename does not match the type name (EntitlementResolver vs Entitlement) per Google Swift Style Guide file-names rule. Fix: rename the file to Entitlement.swift, or rename the enum to EntitlementResolver. Other multi-type files in scope (NotificationDispatcher.swift, ProfileActivation.swift, AdReporting.swift, SocialDebugRoute.swift, SocialService.swift, DerivedImportance.swift, and the *Expansion/ DTO-collection files like SubscriptionEntitlement.swift, SemanticSimilarity.swift, Advertising.swift, MarketData.swift, FollowNotifications.swift) declare two or more top-level types each and so fall outside this rule's narrow trigger ("exactly one large type"); all remaining files' primary/sole declared type matches their basename. entries.detail: Ran `grep -nE '^extension '` plus a top-level-declaration scan (struct/class/enum/protocol/extension/actor) over every .swift file in all eight target directories. Only three files had any top-level extension: NotificationFanOut.swift (extends its own co-declared enum NotificationFanOut, fine), NotificationDispatcher.swift (extends Application, but the file also declares `enum NotificationDispatcher` and `class FanOutQueue` as primary types, so it is not an extension-only file and the rule's naming clause does not apply), and EntitlementResolver+DB.swift. The latter's only top-level declarations (lines 13, 18, 86, 151) are four `extension` blocks, all to type `Entitlement` (one to the nested `Entitlement.Tier`) — confirmed by `grep -n "EntitlementResolver"` on the file returning zero code hits, only the filename and a prose comment on line 5. Per the rule, a file of multiple extensions to one type must be named `<TypeName>+...`; the extended type here is `Entitlement`, not `EntitlementResolver`, so the basename should be `Entitlement+DB.swift` (or similar), not `EntitlementResolver+DB.swift`. Offending text: `extension Entitlement.Tier {` (line 13) through the file's remaining `extension Entitlement {` blocks, all under the mismatched basename `EntitlementResolver+DB.swift`. Fix: rename the file to `Entitlement+DB.swift` (or `Entitlement+Resolver.swift` if the resolver association should stay legible), matching the actually-extended type.
entries.rule_title: Conformance-only extension files are named Type+Protocol.swift

entries.detail: Ran `grep -n "^import"` and a symbol grep across all 59 .swift files under the 8 target directories, then read the flagged files directly. entries.detail: Checked every .swift file over ~100 lines in the eight target paths for MARK-delimited, explainable member ordering (grep -n for func/struct/class/enum/extension plus grep -c "// MARK:" per file). EntitlementResolver+DB.swift is 307 lines with zero `// MARK:` comments and mixes unrelated concerns with no stated grouping: entitlement/tier resolution (`Entitlement.Tier.rank` line 14, `Entitlement.tier(fromProductID:)` line 21, `Entitlement.resolve` line 29), then `RequirementExclusion.cost` (line 56), `MemberAlgorithm.serving` (line 81), more `Entitlement` extension members (lines 88-116), `GatedRoutes` (line 117), then abruptly ~15 unrelated Content DTO structs for questionnaires/browse/venue (`BrowseContextDTO` line 168 through `VenueExclusionWarning` line 302) that have nothing to do with entitlements. Offending text at line 168: `struct BrowseContextDTO: Content { let contextID: UUID; let adoptionCount: Int }` -- this begins an unrelated block of questionnaire/browse/venue DTOs appended after the entitlement logic with no `// MARK:` separator, reading as accretion-by-addition rather than a planned order. Fix: split the file (entitlement/tier resolution stays in EntitlementResolver+DB.swift; move the DTO structs to a QuestionnaireDTOs.swift / VenueDTOs.swift), or at minimum add `// MARK: - Entitlement Resolution`, `// MARK: - Gated Routes`, and `// MARK: - Questionnaire/Browse/Venue DTOs` to separate the groups. Other files in scope also lack MARKs (SubscriptionService.swift, NotificationDispatcher.swift, ProfileResolver.swift, MatchmakingProfileModel.swift, ProfileActivation.swift, AuthorVisibilityService.swift, QuestionnaireStatsService.swift, DerivedImportance.swift, SocialDebugRoute.swift, AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel.swift, AkinAPI.swift, QuestionnaireDetailView.swift, SocialDTOs.swift, FollowNotifications.swift, MatchmakingProfile.swift) but their member counts and grouping read as small/coherent enough (e.g. SubscriptionService.swift's 5 static funcs follow subscribe/unsubscribe/mute/list/get lifecycle order) that this file is the clearest, most defensible single offense to flag rather than padding the report with borderline cases.

entries.detail:
Rule SW-GS-027 (Google Swift Style Guide line-wrapping: single-line-if-it-fits) is violated by four function declarations that are wrapped across 4 lines but fit on one line at well under the 100-column limit. I read each file directly and reflowed the declaration by hand to measure the joined width: (1) ProfileService.swift:118-121 `static func delete(
 _ profileID: UUID,
 owner: UUID,
 on database: any Database
) async throws {` -> single line `static func delete(_ profileID: UUID, owner: UUID, on database: any Database) async throws {` is 96 chars. (2) ProfileActivation.swift:80-83 `static func activate(...)` -> single line is 98 chars. (3) AuthorVisibility/AuthorDisclosure.swift:28-31 `static func creatorID(creator: UUID, visibility: AuthorVisibility, viewer: UUID)` -> single line is 95 chars. (4) AuthorDisclosure.swift:50-53, the raw-string overload `static func creatorID(creator: UUID, rawVisibility: String, viewer: UUID) -> UUID? {` -> single line is 88 chars. All four are pure mechanical unwraps (no other change needed) and all land at 88-98 characters, under the 100-column limit. Fix for each: collapse the multi-line parameter list onto the `static func ...` line. I scanned all .swift files under the 8 target directories (59 files total: Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility, Matching under akin-server-side; Flows/Social under akin; Subscriptions, Matchmaking, Expansion under AkinFrontBackModels) with a script that detects multi-line parenthesized declarations and computes the reflowed width; these four were the only offenses found across all 59 files. I did not exhaustively hand-check every multi-line construct outside the paren-wrap heuristic (e.g. multi-line closures, chained calls, multi-line if/guard conditions), so there is a residual chance of additional short-fitting wraps my heuristic did not catch, but the four found above are confirmed real violations by direct file read and manual character count.
entries.rule_title: If it fits on one line, put it on one line

entries.detail: Confirmed the rule text against the cited source (google.github.io/swift/#line-wrapping: unbreakable continuation = same indent as original line; vertical comma-delimited list continuation = exactly +2). I wrote a paren-depth tracking script over all 59 .swift files in the eight target directories and manually verified representative hits by reading the surrounding source. Violation is pervasive, not isolated: virtually every multi-line parameter list and vertical comma list in these directories is indented +4 (one full Xcode indent level) from the statement start rather than the required +2. Example read directly: MatchmakingProfile.swift line 43 `public init(` at indent 4, then line 44 `id: UUID,` at indent 8 (delta +4, should be +6/delta+2) through line 49; same pattern repeats at lines 111-116 in the same file. Identical delta=4 vertical-list violations were found and would need fixing in (non-exhaustive, all read via the same script + spot Reads): AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/Subscriptions/FollowNotifications.swift:112-116; AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/Expansion/SubscriptionEntitlement.swift:48-53; akin-server-side/Sources/App/AuthorVisibility/AuthorDisclosure.swift:29-31,51-53; AuthorVisibilityService.swift:59-62,90-93,100-101; akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/ (Allowance.swift, ContextDedup.swift, ContextMedianRecompute.swift, DerivedImportance.swift, EmbeddingBackfill.swift, EntitlementResolver+DB.swift, EntitlementResolver.swift, MatchingAlgorithm.swift, QuestionnaireStatsService.swift, RedundancyExplanation.swift, RequirementEvaluator.swift, RequirementFilteredMatch.swift, VenueExclusion.swift, VenuePreferenceFilter.swift, AlgorithmSelector.swift, AdFeedBuilder.swift); akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matchmaking/ (EffectiveChoices.swift, MatchmakingProfileModel.swift, MedianRecompute.swift, ProfileActivation.swift). Some of these show even larger deltas (+18, +19, +25, +26, +28, +29, +33, +37) where continuation lines are aligned to the open parenthesis column instead of +2, which the rule also explicitly forbids. Fix for the cited example: reindent lines 44-49 of MatchmakingProfile.swift from 8 spaces to 6 spaces (statement indent 4 + 2).
entries.rule_title: Continuation indentation is +0 for unbreakable, +2 for vertical list members

entries.detail: Rule applies (Swift, 59 .swift files across all 8 target dirs). Ran: (1) `grep -rn "^[[:space:]]*{[[:space:]]*$"` across all targets: zero matches, meaning no file ever puts an opening brace on its own line. (2) `grep -rn -A1 "&&\s*$\|\|\|\s*$"` and a guard-wrap search (`^\s*guard$`): zero matches, meaning no wrapped boolean/guard conditions exist to trigger the +2-indent own-line case. (3) A python scan of all 59 files that walks every line starting a func/init/struct/if/guard/switch or ending in `,`/`(` with unbalanced parens, gathers continuation lines up to the one ending in `{`, and compares that line's indent delta against the original declaration's indent, flagging delta==2-with-same-line-brace or delta!=2-with-own-line-brace: zero flags. (4) Manually verified two concrete wrapped-signature examples by reading source: akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matchmaking/ProfileSelectionModel.swift:50-59 (`init(` at indent 4, params at indent 8, closing `) {` back at indent 4, delta 0, brace on same line, correct per rule) and akin/akin/Flows/Social/AkinAPI.swift:78-84 (`func send<Body: Encodable, Reply: Decodable>(` at indent 4, params at indent 8, `) async throws -> Reply {` at indent 4, delta 0, same-line brace, correct). Every wrapped declaration in scope is a parameter list whose closing paren returns to the original line's indentation (delta 0), which correctly keeps the brace on that final line; the +2-indent trigger for an own-line brace never occurs in this scope, and no own-line brace ever appears. No offenses found.

entries.detail: Ran `grep -rn "where" --include="*.swift"` (excluding comment lines) across all 8 target directories (59 total .swift files: akin-server-side/Sources/App/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,AuthorVisibility,Matching} - 36 files, akin/akin/Flows/Social - 13 files, AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,Expansion} - 10 files). Neither exceeds 100 columns in a way that would trigger the wrap rule even if it applied, and no declaration anywhere in scope has a generic constraint where clause at all (wrapped or unwrapped). The artifact this rule checks for is entirely absent from these targets.

entries.detail: Ran targeted greps across all 59 .swift files under the eight target directories for `func ` declarations spanning multiple lines (find results saved to /tmp/swfiles.txt; candidates isolated by unmatched paren counts / missing brace on the func line). Verified against Google's Swift style guide function-declaration section (fetched live from google.github.io/swift/#function-declarations): a wrapped declaration's formal argument list must break right after the opening parenthesis, with every parameter on its own line at a +2 hanging indent and the closing paren on its own line before the return type; no parameter stays on the func-name line once wrapping is needed. Fourteen declarations in the target scope instead keep the first parameter on the func line and vertically column-align subsequent parameters under it (the Xcode auto-indent convention, not Google's), which is exactly what the row's own deterministic_tools mapping (SwiftLint `multiline_parameters`) flags. Confirmed by direct read (sed -n) of each: akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/RequirementEvaluator.swift:17 `public static func evaluate(flavor: RequirementFlavor,` (5 more params column-aligned on lines 18-22); same pattern at VenueExclusion.swift:16, AdFeedBuilder.swift:35, RedundancyExplanation.swift:26, AlgorithmSelector.swift:41 and :49, ContextDedup.swift:20, Allowance.swift:25, VenuePreferenceFilter.swift:26, RequirementFilteredMatch.swift:24. By contrast, akin/akin/Flows/Social/AkinAPI.swift:80 and :99 correctly follow the guide's pattern (no parameter on the func line, hanging indent, closing paren on its own line) and every other file checked in Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility, AkinFrontBackModels, and the rest of Flows/Social either fits on one line or wraps correctly. I also specifically searched (and found zero matches) for the narrower example in the prompt itself: a func name split from its own opening parenthesis, a lone `->` on its own line, or a standalone `where` clause. So the real, repeated offense in scope is the mixed first-param-on-declaration-line plus vertically-aligned continuation, not the name/paren split example.
entries.rule_title: Wrapped function declarations follow the standard partition

entries.detail: Ran `grep -rnE '(class|struct|enum|protocol|extension)\b.*:' ` across all 8 target directories (akin-server-side/Sources/App/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,AuthorVisibility,Matching}, akin/akin/Flows/Social, AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,Expansion}) and inspected every type/extension declaration with an inheritance list (~90 hits, e.g. akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matchmaking/ProfileSelectionModel.swift:13 `final class ProfileSelectionModel: @unchecked Sendable, Model, Content {`, AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/Expansion/Advertising.swift:54 `public struct AdCampaign: Codable, Hashable, Identifiable {`). Ran `swiftlint lint --no-cache` over all 8 directories and grepped output for inherit/wrap: no results. Since no wrapped type/extension declaration exists anywhere in scope, there is no inheritance list that could be half-horizontal/half-vertical and no constraint list that could be broken at the wrong delimiter, so the rule holds.

entries.detail: Read /Users/scottlydon/Developer/akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/RequirementFilteredMatch.swift lines 28-32. The wrapped call `RequirementEvaluator.evaluate(` opens at line 29 (indent 12). Its two continuation lines each carry three arguments instead of one: line 30 `flavor: r.flavor, requirementContextID: r.contextID, matchingContextID: input.contextID,` and line 31 `questionID: r.questionID, responseIDs: r.responseIDs, candidateAnswers: candidateAnswers)`. A second, related pattern (wrong continuation indent, though only one arg per continuation line) recurs at akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/EntitlementResolver+DB.swift lines 133-147, six `.init(...)` array-literal calls whose second line (e.g. line 134 `pathTemplate: "api/user/{user}/requirements"),`) is vertically aligned to column 14 instead of indented +2 (10) from the 8-space-indented opening line. I checked all 59 .swift files across the eight given target directories (akin-server-side/Sources/App/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,AuthorVisibility,Matching}, akin/akin/Flows/Social, AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,Expansion}) via ripgrep for comma-then-label patterns and manually inspected each multi-line call candidate; the rest of the wrapped calls found (MatchingAlgorithm.swift init, NotificationPusher.swift APNSAlertNotification) correctly place one parameter per continuation line.
entries.rule_title: Wrapped call arguments each get their own line at +2

entries.detail: Rule SW-GS-035 (Google Swift Style Guide: a wrapped trailing-closure signature must go on its own line with the arg list parenthesized). Enumerated all 59 .swift files in the 8 target directories (via find), then ran targeted searches: (1) grep -n -E '\bin$' across all files to find every trailing-closure signature line ending in `in` (22 hits, e.g. akin-server-side/Sources/App/Subscriptions/SubscriptionService.swift:140,146, NotificationPusher.swift:31, Matchmaking/ProfileActivation.swift:112, Matching/VenueExclusion.swift:20, AdFeedBuilder.swift:45, EntitlementResolver+DB.swift:66, DerivedImportance.swift:93,112, akin/akin/Flows/Social/SocialDebugRoute.swift:141,210, SubscriptionsView.swift:31,38, ProfileSwitcherView.swift:37,51, QuestionnaireDetailView.swift:44,62,134, QuestionnaireBrowseView.swift:32) and inspected each: every one is a single-line trailing closure of the form `foo(...) { param, param2 in` with the entire signature on the same line as the call (e.g. `.reduce(into: [UUID: String]()) { map, row in`, `database.transaction { transaction in`, `ForEach(questionnaires, id: \\.self) { entry in`). (2) An awk pass over all 59 files specifically looking for a `{` at end of a line immediately followed by a closure-signature line ending in ` in` (the pattern the rule targets: signature wrapped onto its own line) returned zero matches. No file in scope has a trailing closure whose signature was wrapped across multiple lines at all, parenthesized or not, so the rule's precondition (a wrapped signature) never occurs in this scope; there is nothing to flag as unparenthesized. Zero offenses found, consistent with the agent_prompt's own PASS criterion.
entries.rule_title: A wrapped trailing-closure signature goes on its own line with the arg list parenthesized

entries.detail: Ran python3 to compute indent columns for every multi-line `guard` in the eight target trees (59 .swift files total under /Users/scottlydon/Developer/{akin-server-side/Sources/App/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,AuthorVisibility,Matching}, akin/akin/Flows/Social, AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,Expansion}}), comparing each continuation line's leading-space count against the column of the token following `guard` (indent + 6 for "guard "). No wrapped if/while/for statements exist in scope (grep for lines ending in &&, ||, or , after if/while/for returned nothing), and no `guard`'s `else` is split onto its own line (checked with a regex for `^\s*else\s*\{\s*$` across all 59 files, zero hits), so that half of the rule holds. But two guard statements wrap their condition via method chaining and misalign: in ProfileResolver.swift, `guard let winner = try await MatchmakingProfileModel.query(on: database)` starts at column 12, so the post-keyword token `let` sits at column 18; the chained continuation lines 132-135 (`.filter(\.$ownerID == owner)`, `.filter(\.$contextID == contextID)`, `.filter(\.$isDefault == true)`, `.first() else {`) are indented to column 16, two columns short of the required alignment. The same misalignment recurs in akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/EntitlementResolver+DB.swift:157-159, where `guard let sub = ...` starts at column 8 (post-keyword `let` at column 14) but the `.filter(...)` continuation lines sit at column 16 — and inconsistently, that guard's own trailing condition line 160 (`sub.expiresAt == nil ...`) IS correctly aligned to column 14, showing the file mixes both conventions in the same statement. Fix for line 132 (and 133-135 identically): re-indent each continuation line from 16 spaces to 18 spaces so `.filter`/`.first()` starts under `let`.
entries.rule_title: Wrapped control flow aligns to the token after the keyword; guard keeps `else {` together

entries.detail: Ran `grep -n -B1 -E '^\s*(&&|\|\|)' ` over all 59 .swift files under the 8 target directories, plus checks for trailing `&&`/`||`/`=`/ternary line-wraps; the only wrapped non-call expression found is in AdFeedBuilder.swift. Measured indentation with python3 (len minus lstrip): line 46 `campaign.targetedQuestionIDs.contains(questionID)` is indented 16 spaces, and its continuation line 47 `&& (memberMatch[campaign.campaignID] ?? 0) >= campaign.minProfileMatch` is indented 20 spaces, i.e. +4 from the original line, not the +2 the Google Swift Style Guide rule requires for wrapped non-call (boolean chain) expressions. Fix: dedent line 47 to 18 spaces (16 + 2). No other wrapped non-call expressions (boolean chains, ternaries, trailing `=`) were found in the remaining files across Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility, Matching, Flows/Social, and the three FrontBackModels directories.
entries.rule_title: Other wrapped expressions indent the second line exactly +2

entries.detail: Searched all 8 target directories for if/guard/while/switch statements with opening parenthesis. Found 3 matches total (1 if, 2 guard): EmbeddingBackfill.swift:32 `if (existing?.n ?? 0) > 0 {`, AkinAPI.swift:127 `guard (200..<300).contains(http.statusCode) else {`, and AdFeedBuilder.swift:42 `guard (index + 1) % cadence == 0 else {`. entries.detail: Searched all .swift files under the 8 target dirs (akin-server-side/Sources/App/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,AuthorVisibility,Matching}, akin/akin/Flows/Social, AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,Expansion}) for the three flagged ambiguity patterns: (1) && mixed with || on one expression via grep -E '&&.*\|\||\|\|.*&&' and a broader grep -l '&&\|||' pass narrowing to 3 files (AdFeedBuilder.swift, EntitlementResolver+DB.swift, VenuePreferenceFilter.swift); (2) bit shifts (<<, >>) mixed with arithmetic, zero matches in any target file; (3) ?? mixed with comparison operators (==, !=, <, >) via grep -E '\?\?.*(==|!=|<|>)|(==|!=|<|>).*\?\?'. Read each hit in context: EntitlementResolver+DB.swift:31/95 already parenthesizes the || group inside the && (`$0.revokedAt == nil && ($0.expiresAt == nil || $0.expiresAt! > now)`); AdFeedBuilder.swift:47 parenthesizes the ?? default before comparing (`(memberMatch[campaign.campaignID] ?? 0) >= campaign.minProfileMatch`); VenuePreferenceFilter.swift:30 uses only && with no ||; the other ?? hits (EntitlementResolver+DB.swift:82,89,96; ContextMedianRecompute.swift:35; EmbeddingBackfill.swift:32; QuestionnaireDetailView.swift:90) are plain fallback-then-return or fallback-then-method-chain expressions, never combined with a bare comparison operator at the same precedence level. entries.detail: Ran a def-use distance scan (python3, custom brace-tracking script) over all 58 .swift files found under the 8 target directories (find ... -name "*.swift"), checking every function body longer than 25 lines for local let/var declarations whose first subsequent use is >15 lines away. Five hits surfaced and I read each in context: NotificationPusher.swift:36,39 (sent/notification) — the apparent gap is just a multi-line APNSAlertNotification initializer, not hoisting; ContextMedianRecompute.swift:22 (contextSet) — correctly precomputed once before a loop that reuses it every iteration, the idiomatic placement; ContextMedianRecompute.swift:32 and EmbeddingBackfill.swift:24 (both named written) — standard `var written = 0` accumulator declared immediately before the loop that increments it, already minimally scoped. No declaration in the scanned files is hoisted away from its first use in violation of the rule; the codebase (Vapor server routes/services, SwiftUI viewmodels/views, and DTO model files) consistently declares locals immediately before use or as loop-invariant precomputations directly preceding the loop that consumes them.

entries.detail: Checked every enum under the eight target directories (found via `find ... -name "*.swift" | xargs grep -n "enum "` then read each case list). Almost all follow a defensible ordering: lifecycle order (VenueNegotiation.swift NegotiationState: proposed, countered, accepted, declined), paired subscribe/unsubscribe-then-guards (SubscriptionError.swift), or screen-grouped (SocialDebugRoute.swift SocialDebugState: browse*, detail*, subscriptions*, profiles*). One enum breaks the rule: `Entitlement.Capability` in akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/EntitlementResolver.swift:19-25 (`case createContext, chooseVenues, blacklistVenues, negotiateVenues, unlimitedFreezes, unlimitedNearbyMeetups, reservations, compatibilityVisibility, algorithmChoice, additionalContexts, requiredQuestions, matchmakingProfiles`) groups the first six cases by theme (context, three venue cases, two freeze/meetup cases) but the remaining six (reservations, compatibilityVisibility, algorithmChoice, additionalContexts, requiredQuestions, matchmakingProfiles) are singletons with no shared theme, no numeric/raw-value order, and no alphabetical order (alphabetical would be additionalContexts, algorithmChoice, blacklistVenues, chooseVenues, compatibilityVisibility, createContext, matchmakingProfiles, negotiateVenues, requiredQuestions, reservations, unlimitedFreezes, unlimitedNearbyMeetups). Per the rule's own fallback, this tail should be lexicographic. The identical enum is duplicated at AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/Expansion/SubscriptionEntitlement.swift:8-19 (`public enum Capability: String, Codable, CaseIterable, Hashable { case createContext / case chooseVenues / ... / case requiredQuestions }`, missing matchmakingProfiles) with the same non-alphabetical, non-grouped tail. Fix: reorder both enums' cases lexicographically (or, if the intent is chronological/feature-swath order, add a comment stating that scheme so a reader can verify it, since chronological-by-swath-item is not visually distinguishable from "no ordering" without one).
entries.rule_title: Enum cases follow a logical ordering, else lexicographic

entries.detail: Ran `grep -nE '@escaping|\(\s*\(.*\)\s*->|completion:|onComplete|handler:|perform:'` across all 59 .swift files in the eight target directories (akin-server-side/Sources/App/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,AuthorVisibility,Matching}, akin/akin/Flows/Social, AkinFrontBackModels/Sources/FrontBackModels/{Subscriptions,Matchmaking,Expansion}). entries.detail: Ran targeted grep for `(var|let) name: Bool` across all 8 target directories, then read each hit in context with sed. Apple's guideline "boolean properties/types read as assertions (isEmpty)" is violated by a recurring `muted: Bool` field used for the same mute-state concept in three places: akin-server-side/Sources/App/Subscriptions/SubscriptionError.swift:70 (`let muted: Bool` in struct SetMutedRequest, doc comment "True to silence the subscription, false to hear it again") and :87 (same struct field on SubscriptionListEntry), and the mirrored client-side DTO akin/akin/Flows/Social/SocialDTOs.swift:94 (SubscriptionEntry) and :117 (SetMutedBody). By contrast the sibling `isActive`/`isDefault`/`isRated`/`isPaywalled`/`isAd`/`isTerminal` Bool properties found in the same sweep (e.g. akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matchmaking/MatchmakingProfileModel.swift:37,46 and akin/akin/Flows/Social/SocialDTOs.swift:105-106) already comply and are not flagged. A local `let rated: Bool` at akin/akin/Flows/Social/SocialDebugRoute.swift:124 is a function-local binding, not a declaration, so I did not flag it separately.

entries.detail: Audited 59 Swift files across 8 target directories, analyzing 80 type definitions. entries.detail: Ran rg across all eight target directories for -1/Int.max/"NONE"/"UNKNOWN" style sentinels and for non-optional Int/Double/String-returning functions, then read the surrounding file. Line 25: `var sortKey: Double { if case .score(let value) = self { return value } else { return -1 } }` returns -1 as a non-optional Double to signal the `.unrated` case, distinguishable from a real score only because callers happen to know the valid range starts at ImportanceScale.minimum (1). The type system does not encode that guarantee: sortKey's signature promises a plain Double, so any future scale change (e.g. a minimum <= -1, or someone reusing sortKey outside a sort context) would silently misread "unrated" as a real, very-low score. Fix: make sortKey return `Double?` (nil for `.unrated`), and have the sort call site do `.sorted { ($0.sortKey ?? -.infinity) < ($1.sortKey ?? -.infinity) }` or equivalent, keeping the "no rating" case out of Double's domain entirely rather than encoding it as -1. This is the only offense found in the eight scoped directories; other non-optional-returning functions checked (counts, scores, text builders in AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel, QuestionnaireStatsService, EntitlementResolver+DB, etc.) return genuine values with no magic-value absence signaling in their docs, comments, or call sites.

entries.detail: Ran targeted greps across all eight target dirs for tuple/Result/Bool-plus-out-param error-encoding patterns (`func .* -> (`, `Result<...,String>`, `-> (Bool`, `inout ... String?`, `errorCode`/`reasonCode`) and manually read every hit. Two other Bool-returning functions surfaced (AdReporting.swift:36 `record(token:)` and AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel.swift:58 `needsConfirmation`) but neither encodes multiple failure reasons: `record` is an idempotency check (false = "already seen", one state, no ambiguity) and `needsConfirmation` is a pure predicate with no failure semantics at all, so they don't offend this rule. VenueNegotiation.swift:54 `public mutating func send(_ event: NegotiationEvent, at: Date) -> Bool` does offend it: the guard at line 55 (`guard !state.isTerminal else { return false }`) and the guard at line 59 (`guard let venue = state.venue else { return false }`) are two distinct, unrelated rejection reasons (negotiation already closed vs. accept issued with no venue on the table) collapsed into the same `false`, so the caller can never distinguish which happened. Fix: replace the Bool return with `throws` and a `NegotiationError` enum, e.g. `enum NegotiationError: Error { case alreadyTerminal, noVenueToAccept }`, throwing the specific case at each guard instead of returning `false`, and changing the signature to `public mutating func send(_ event: NegotiationEvent, at: Date) throws(NegotiationError)`.
entries.rule_title: Multiple error states throw an Error type

The same pattern (undocumented public struct/enum/let/init) recurs in AdProfileScorer.swift:12, AdReporting.swift:12/16/21/33/34/36, AlgorithmSelector.swift:19-38, Allowance.swift:12-22, CompatibilityVisibility.swift:12, ContextDedup.swift:13, EntitlementResolver.swift:15-51, MatchingAlgorithm.swift:19-35, PercentileAlgorithm.swift:15-20, RedundancyExplanation.swift:14-23, RequirementEvaluator.swift:13-15, RequirementFilteredMatch.swift:11-21, VenueExclusion.swift:12, VenueNegotiation.swift:13-46, VenuePreferenceFilter.swift:13-23 in Matching, and Advertising.swift, MarketData.swift, MatchingAlgorithmChoice.swift:5, QuestionRequirement.swift:5, SemanticSimilarity.swift, SubscriptionEntitlement.swift:32, VenuePreference.swift in AkinFrontBackModels/Expansion. Fix: add a /// doc comment above each undocumented public/open declaration and stored property/initializer explaining its purpose (e.g. for AdCampaignPlacement: '/// A campaign's targeting and minimum-match requirement for one in-feed ad slot.'), per Google Swift Style Guide 'Where to Document'. Enumerated all 61 .swift files under the 8 target directories (Subscriptions, Matchmaking, AuthorVisibility, Matching in akin-server-side; Flows/Social in akin; Subscriptions, Matchmaking, Expansion in AkinFrontBackModels). Ran a python clustering script parsing every line as either a method call `receiver.method(args)` or property assignment `receiver.prop = value`, grouping consecutive lines by (kind, method/prop) first with args also required equal (strict) then with args ignored (loose) - both passes found zero runs of length >= 2. Also grepped directly for the classic UIKit trigger patterns (addTarget, .font =, translatesAutoresizingMaskIntoConstraints, addSubview) across all target dirs: 0 matches. This is expected: the Flows/Social files are SwiftUI views/viewmodels (no imperative UIKit setup code) and the akin-server-side/AkinFrontBackModels files are Vapor backend services and Fluent models, not view code with repeated per-view setter calls. No offending consecutive-statement runs found in scope.

entries.detail: Ran an awk pass over every *.swift file under the eight target directories flagging `func` declarations with no `///` line immediately above, then manually re-checked each hit against surrounding context to rule out attribute lines (e.g. @discardableResult) and enclosing-type doc comments that legitimately cover a sole method (confirmed false positives in VenueNegotiation.swift:54, ContextMedianRecompute.swift:19, EntitlementResolver+DB.swift:56/81, and others, all of which do have a genuine covering comment). One hit survives: `static func score(ratingsByQuestion:) -> DerivedImportance` at DerivedImportance.swift:108 has zero comment of its own. Quoted text: `static func score(ratingsByQuestion: [UUID: [Double]]) -> DerivedImportance {` followed by a body that reimplements the Bayesian-shrinkage formula `(n * ownMean + k * populationMean) / (n + k)` inline, independently of the sibling method `breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:)` at line 90 which computes the identical formula per-question. The file's own doc comment on `breakdown` (lines 71-74) explicitly warns: "Returned rather than recomputed on the client... A second implementation... would drift from this one, and the drift would be invisible: both would look like plausible percentages." `score` is exactly that second implementation, uncommented, inside the same file that names the risk. This is a genuine WTF moment for a reader: why does `score` not call `breakdown` and sum/average its `shrunk` values instead of duplicating the math? Fix: either (a) rewrite `score` to call `breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:)` and average `.shrunk` over the results (eliminates the duplication and the drift risk entirely), or if duplication is intentional for performance, add a doc comment explaining why it does not reuse `breakdown` and noting the two must be kept in sync. I did not check every one of the ~59 swift files exhaustively (economical-search constraint); I concentrated on Matching, Subscriptions, AuthorVisibility, and Matchmaking under akin-server-side per the awk sweep, and spot-read the flagged candidates. AkinFrontBackModels/Expansion, akin/Flows/Social, and AkinFrontBackModels/Subscriptions and Matchmaking (small dirs, 1-13 files each) were listed by the sweep but no candidate from them survived the attribute/enclosing-comment re-check, so I am not separately re-verifying each as a pass beyond that sweep.

(2) AuthorVisibilityPickerViewModel.swift:103 `func cancelPending() { pendingDisclosure = nil }` -> called only as an ordinary method (`model.cancelPending()` in akinTests/SocialViewModelTests.swift:420), never as a function reference, so per the rule it should be removed and `pendingDisclosure = nil` inlined at its one call site. Other single-statement Void-shaped hits were checked and excluded as legitimate protocol requirements: `revert(on:)` in ProfileSelectionModel.swift:90 and MatchmakingProfileModel.swift:105 implement Fluent's `Migration` protocol, and `subscribe`/`unsubscribe` in SocialService.swift:76/80 implement the `SocialServing` protocol declared at lines 19-20 of the same file.

entries.detail: Ran the rule's detector (regex over local `let` decls in the 8 target dirs, cross-checked each candidate's usage count and call-site context by hand) across all *.swift files under the eight target paths (akin-server-side Subscriptions/Matchmaking/AuthorVisibility/Matching, akin/Flows/Social, AkinFrontBackModels Subscriptions/Matchmaking/Expansion). Most single-textual-occurrence `let`s I found were false positives once inspected: they're either stored struct properties (no violation, not local vars used once "at the point of use"), or locals hoisted out of a loop/closure to avoid recomputation each iteration (e.g. ContextMedianRecompute.swift's contextSet/choicesByUser, EffectiveChoices.swift's overridden, EntitlementResolver+DB.swift's answers, QuestionnaireStatsService.swift's wanted, ProfileService.swift's wasActive which must be captured before a delete() call) or would hurt readability if inlined into a guard/if condition spanning a multi-line query chain. One genuine violation survived: VenueExclusion.swift:19, `let minePruned = candidates.subtracting(blockedByMember)`, referenced exactly once at line 21 inside `reduce`, with no loop-hoisting or perf rationale (it's a top-level statement in a static func body, not inside a loop). Inlined form: `blockedByOthers.values.reduce(0) { acc, theirs in candidates.subtracting(blockedByMember).subtracting(theirs).isEmpty ? acc + 1 : acc }` (95 chars including indent for the inner line, well under any reasonable column limit, and arguably reads better as one chained set-subtraction). Output line: `/Users/scottlydon/Developer/akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/VenueExclusion.swift:19 - let minePruned = candidates.subtracting(blockedByMember) -> inline as candidates.subtracting(blockedByMember).subtracting(theirs).isEmpty ? acc + 1 : acc on line 21, deleting line 19`.

The rule flags static methods declared directly ON a Fluent Model type; these are already factored into separate service/helper namespace types, the pattern the rule wants, not static methods on the Model itself. No offense found.

entries.detail: Checked the most recent commits touching the swath (git log -5 on each target dir, then `git show` on the newest commit per dir to diff for added `func`s: akin-server-side commit bd1b4db added DerivedImportance.swift's `breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:)`, and the same file already has `score(ratingsByQuestion:)`. Read the full file. `static func score(ratingsByQuestion: [UUID: [Double]]) -> DerivedImportance` (line 108) reimplements, inline, the exact per-question shrinkage arithmetic (`clamped`, `n`, `ownMean`, `k`, `(n*ownMean + k*populationMean)/(n+k)`) that `static func breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:) -> [QuestionBreakdown]` (line 92) already computes and returns per question as `shrunk`. `score` -> Sum(shrunk)/count would produce the same result as calling `breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:).map(\.shrunk).reduce(0,+) / Double(breakdown(...).count)` (guarding for the unrated case first). Fix: `score` should call `breakdown(ratingsByQuestion:)` and average its `.shrunk` values instead of recomputing clamp/mean/shrinkage a second time, e.g. `DerivedImportance.swift:108 - let perQuestion: [Double] = rated.values.map { ratings in ... } -> replace with DerivedImportanceCalculator.breakdown(ratingsByQuestion: rated).map { $0.shrunk }`. Also checked the other targets' newest commits for new funcs (akin client 9687c0fa added `text(for:in:)` and `workingText(for:)` in QuestionnaireDetailView.swift; server 27afd05 touched Subscriptions/Matching/AuthorVisibility but its diff added no new `func` in those dirs) and did not find comparable duplication there. Coverage note: I only diffed each target directory's single most-recent commit for new funcs, not every historical addition, per the economical-search constraint; this finding is the one clear duplicate located within that scope.

entries.detail: Audited SW-PP-003 (every failure case throws a clear, comprehensive, specific error) against all 8 target dirs. Found and read every Error enum/struct: SubscriptionError (akin-server-side/Sources/App/Subscriptions/SubscriptionError.swift:17-56), ProfileError (Matchmaking/ProfileActivation.swift:12-58), AuthorVisibilityError (AuthorVisibility/AuthorVisibilityService.swift:13-37, plus throw AuthorVisibilityError.questionNotFound/notTheCreator and a guarded Abort at line 132 with a specific reason), AllowanceExceeded (Matching/Allowance.swift:12-19) and AllVenuesBlockedError (Matching/VenuePreferenceFilter.swift:13-20) — both CustomStringConvertible structs embedding the offending ids/counts in their description — and AkinAPIError (akin/akin/Flows/Social/AkinAPI.swift:26-38, cases refused(status,reason)/unreachable(detail)/unreadable(detail)). All 4 bare `Abort(...)` calls carry a specific `reason:` string (AuthorVisibilityService.swift:132, ProfileService.swift:224, EntitlementResolver+DB.swift:110, EmbeddingBackfill.swift:21). Every `catch {` block that discards the typed error (NotificationFanOut.swift, NotificationDispatcher.swift, ProfileResolver.swift, all 5 SwiftUI ViewModels in akin/akin/Flows/Social) still re-derives a message from the caught error (AkinAPIError.errorDescription, error.localizedDescription, or a `message(error)` helper) before storing/logging it with recipient/question ids attached — none discard the underlying error. The 5 ViewModel `case failed(String)` phases matched the rule's named example pattern literally, but each is populated at the catch site from the real underlying AkinAPIError description (verified in QuestionnaireBrowseViewModel.swift:43, QuestionnaireDetailViewModel.swift:41, SubscriptionsViewModel.swift:39/70/79), so they are not context-free generic errors. No fatalError, no `catch _` (discard pattern), and no `case unknown`/`case error` construct exists in any of the 8 target directories. Rule holds across scope; no offense to report.</detail>

entries.detail: Ran rg -n -U 'catch\s*\{[^}]*\}' and rg -n 'try\?' across all eight target dirs. Most catch blocks are legitimate (throw, or are retry-loop event boundaries in NotificationDispatcher.swift/NotificationFanOut.swift that correctly catch-log-continue per the carveout). One real offense in persistence/matching code: akin-server-side/Sources/App/Matching/ContextMedianRecompute.swift:35 `let sample = Set(members.filter { ((try? $0.requireID()) ?? UUID()) != memberID })` and line 37 `let sampleChoices = sample.flatMap { choicesByUser[(try? $0.requireID()) ?? UUID()] ?? [] }` -> both swallow a requireID() failure via try? and substitute a random UUID() instead of throwing, inside the median-recompute job that writes ContextCompatibilityMedians rows read back for matchmaking percentiles. A failed requireID() (e.g. an unsaved/detached model slipping in) silently produces a fabricated UUID that will never equal any real member or choice key, corrupting the sample set and median arrays with no error surfaced, rather than throwing as the rule requires for persistence-boundary failures. Fix: `guard let id = try? member.requireID() else { throw ... }` (or let requireID() throw un-caught) instead of defaulting to UUID(). I also inspected akin/akin/Flows/Social/AkinAPI.swift:142 `return try? JSONDecoder().decode(Refusal.self, from: data).reason` (a decode-boundary try?) but judged it not an offense: the enclosing call already unconditionally throws AkinAPIError.refused with a hardcoded fallback message regardless of whether this nested reason-decode succeeds, so no failure is silently absorbed there, only a message is best-effort enriched.
entries.rule_title: No catch-log-continue at network and decode boundaries
